clue.text: But the blooming thing didn't really reach to heaven!

definitions.text: But the blooming thing didn't really reach to heaven!

parts.words: But the blooming thing didn't really reach to heaven
parts.note: a flowering garden plant shares its name with the ladder Jacob dreamt of in Genesis, which did stretch up to heaven; the plant only borrowed the name

explanation.surface: A wry aside about a flower that failed to climb all the way up to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a blue-flowered border plant (Polemonium) and the biblical ladder seen in Jacob's dream reaching into heaven.

clue.text: Stimulate would-be revolutionary to exercise

parts.note: to jog the memory is to stimulate it
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger who would like a revolution

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to rouse a would-be revolutionary into taking some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady slow running pace is a form of physical training, so the word stands for exercise taken at that gait.

clue.text: Act like William? Miss Hardcastle stoops to

definitions.meaning: William I of England was known as the Conqueror, so acting like him means overcoming by force
Kate Hardcastle is the heroine of Goldsmith's comedy She Stoops to ..., the title completed by this word

explanation.surface: Two literary teasers: copying a king named William, and what a play's heroine lowers herself to do.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror won England by force, and Goldsmith's play title is She Stoops to Conquer, Kate Hardcastle being the she.

clue.text: Composer caught entering before priestess

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach is the composer
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A composer is arrested on the way in, ahead of a priestess.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchante was a priestess or female follower of Bacchus, the Roman god of wine.

clue.text: Learners copy inside part of suit

indicators.note: inside places the copy within the pair of learners

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, so two learners give two Ls
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: Trainee tailors copy the inside of part of a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back front flap of a jacket, one component of a suit.

clue.text: Girl supports cover-up — a problem for Shaw's doctor

indicators.note: supports means the girl sits next to and holds up the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
in botany a lemma is the outer bract that covers a grass flower

explanation.surface: A girl backs a cover-up, presenting a Shavian medic with a quandary.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's play The Doctor's Dilemma gives the definition; LEMMA is the botanist's word for a bract wrapping a grass floret, hence a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote The Doctor's Dilemma, so the doctor's problem in that title is a quandary between two choices.

clue.text: Meatier concoction for chieftain's office

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of meatier are mixed up

explanation.surface: A richer, meatier dish is cooked up for a tribal chief's headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is the rank, office or territory of an emir, an Arab ruler or chieftain.

clue.text: Mail manager's tension after motorway trip

indicators.note: after places the tension behind the motorway trip

parts.note: post is an old word for a journey made by relays of horses, hence a trip
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
stress is tension or strain

explanation.surface: A post office worker suffers stress after a drive on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, and 'post' as a journey is an old use from travelling by relays of horses; 'after' sets the tension behind the motorway trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmistress is the woman in charge of a local post office, so she manages the mail.

clue.text: The sort of crop I can grow out West, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the remaining letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out means the West letter is removed from grow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer says which kind of crop they can raise out in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes W (West) from GROW, leaving GRO; 'perhaps' then rearranges ICAN plus GRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic describes produce grown without synthetic fertilisers or pesticides, a type of crop.

clue.text: Activity in station generally making one cross?

definitions.text: Activity in station generally making one cross?

parts.words: Activity in station generally making one cross
parts.note: at the place where votes are cast, each voter marks a cross on the ballot paper; the surface suggests an irritated commuter at a railway station

explanation.surface: Something going on at a station that tends to annoy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting takes place at a polling station, where the voter marks the ballot with an X.

clue.text: Amiable party turned up, strengthened after journey

indicators.note: after means the journey piece comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: to go is to travel or journey

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party
tempered steel has been hardened, made stronger

explanation.surface: A friendly celebration arrived, its spirits fortified after the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DO to OD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone good-tempered is easygoing and pleasant, which is what amiable means.

clue.text: Husband fills food container from end to end

indicators.note: fills means the husband goes inside the container

parts.note: a trough holds feed for animals

explanation.surface: A husband stuffs a feeding vessel full from one end to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean all the way along something, from start to finish.

clue.text: Painful condition round ancient Frenchman's back — doctor poked in

indicators.note: poked in means the doctor is pushed inside the reversed word
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Gaul was an inhabitant of ancient France
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A painful ailment afflicts an old Frenchman's back when a medic prods it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the Frenchman round to LUAG, and 'poked in' pushes the doctor inside; 'round' is not a reversal signal here but the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back muscles, a sore medical condition.

clue.text: Lay to rest in Mappin Terraces

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is to be buried at the Mappin Terraces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mappin Terraces are an artificial mountain enclosure at London Zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it, laying the dead to rest.

clue.text: Express delivery, possibly, from one's shop?

definitions.text: Express delivery, possibly, from one's shop?

parts.words: Express delivery, possibly, from one's shop
parts.note: the Daily Express is a British newspaper, so a delivery of it would come from the shop that sells papers, not a courier

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fast courier service might come from your local store.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent sells and delivers newspapers such as the Express, a British daily.

clue.text: Saint in 'small group moving towards sunset

indicators.note: in places the saint inside the other pieces

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
a ring is a group, such as a drugs ring

explanation.surface: A saint in a little band heads off into the sunset.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'small' is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Westering describes something heading west, as the sun does when it goes down.

clue.text: Girl keeps centre of floor covering in poor condition

indicators.note: keeps means the girl holds the other piece inside her

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name

indicators.note: centre of means only the middle of the floor covering is used, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: matting is coarse woven material laid on floors

explanation.surface: A girl holds on to the middle of a worn rug in a shabby state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' trims the floor covering to ATTIN, which 'keeps' holds inside the girl; the 'in' before the definition is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattiness is shabbiness, a worn and run-down state.

clue.text: Reportedly hear engineers build warship

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are said to be building a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY, to hear a case in court, is taken as its sound TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Live in fashionable belt housing upper classes

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: housing means the belt holds the upper classes inside it

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
A and B are the top social grades in British market research

explanation.surface: Smart people live wearing a stylish belt that holds the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to dwell or reside there.

clue.text: Furore as creative writing is short by one mark

indicators.note: short by one means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a story is a piece of imaginative writing
M is the abbreviation for mark, an old German currency

explanation.surface: An uproar arises when a writing assignment falls one mark short.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean an outburst of anger or controversy, as in a storm of protest.

clue.text: Hint of fraud connected with starter

indicators.note: connected with joins the fraud to the starter, which comes first

parts.note: soup is a typical first course
a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: A trace of a scam linked to the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount, a trace or suggestion of something.

clue.text: Instrument originally classified in old lists, say

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other pieces
say signals that the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the lists were the enclosed arena for a jousting tournament

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A musical instrument first catalogued in old inventories.
explanation.walkthrough: ARENA, the lists, is taken by its sound as ARINA; C, the first letter of 'classified', goes in after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Descriptive word from key article used in mine

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: used in means the article goes inside the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A descriptive word is made from a key and an article down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase describing a person or thing.

clue.text: All the players express irritation before half-time

parts.note: tut is a sound of annoyance

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters are taken

explanation.surface: The whole team shows annoyance just before the half-time whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for the whole orchestra or all performers to play together.

clue.text: Try to surpass fast runner no longer with us

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird that runs fast
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Someone tries to beat a sprinter who has since died.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or outdo them.

clue.text: A woman's wager after second drink

indicators.note: after means the woman's wager follows the second

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A woman bets on a second drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherbet is also an old word for a cooling fruit drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet originally meant a cooling Middle Eastern fruit drink, and is still slang for an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Be disposed to lean forward

definitions.meaning: to be ... or minded to do something
to bend or tilt the body forward

explanation.surface: Feel inclined to bend forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To incline is both to feel a leaning towards something and physically to tilt or bend forward.

clue.text: State's unusually striking view a thousand disregarded (4,8) 23,284

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are arranged in an unusual way
disregarded means the thousand letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
K is short for a thousand, as in kilo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US state is said to have a remarkably striking view, if you ignore a thousand things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarded' takes K out of STRIKING; 'unusually' rearranges what remains with VIEW and A. The trailing number is a printed puzzle number, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: West Virginia is one of the fifty United States.
